title: Mapping the Audit Gap: A Coverage Matrix of Governance-Required Properties vs. Verifiable Evidence

original_idea.body:
# Mapping the Audit Gap: A Coverage Matrix of Governance-Required Properties vs. Verifiable Evidence

**Problem:** A position paper formalizes an 'audit gap' between required safety properties and what behavioural assurance can verify, but does not quantify the gap across published evaluation suites.

**Direction:** Build a coverage matrix: extract required-evidence properties from 7 governance instruments, hand-code whether published model cards present behavioural/latent/no evidence, compute per-instrument coverage scores.

**Why it matters:** Turns an abstract claim into an auditable score for regulators. Pure document analysis.

**Relevant context:** Extends arXiv:2605.15164 (May 2026).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: quantifying the audit gap advances third-party verification, a pathway major orgs treat as critical.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: LLM-assisted document coding against governance instruments; guided, no compute.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused coverage-matrix deliverable, though spanning 7 instruments adds breadth.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Pure document analysis, third-party verification labs won't own; independent-friendly.

low_compute.reasoning: Document analysis with light LLM assistance; CPU/free-tier.

novelty.reasoning: The audit-gap concept is published; the empirical coverage scoring is the open extension.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: The concept is published; the empirical coverage matrix is the open extension.
